title: Understanding the Problem
text: The problem involves comparing two linear regression models: one using the original design matrix X and the other using the mean-centered design matrix X̃. Both models aim to minimize the sum of squared errors.

title: Mean-Centering Effect
text: Mean-centering affects the intercept term in the regression model. When the data is mean-centered, the intercept term becomes zero, but the slopes (coefficients) remain unchanged.

title: Comparing Coefficients
text: Since mean-centering does not affect the slopes, the coefficients for the predictors (excluding the intercept) remain the same in both models.

title: Conclusion on Coefficients
text: Given that mean-centering does not change the slopes, are the coefficients for the predictors in both models equal?
